pageCache.pageTitle: Christopher Hatton Primary School - Ethos and Values
pageCache.text:
CHRISTOPHER HATTON ETHOS and VALUES
Our aim is to develop the knowledge, skills and attitudes in our pupils to enable them to become informed, articulate and empowered citizens. We are an inclusive school and are proud to be a beacon of excellence at the heart of our community. ‘Hattoneers’ aim high, respect each other and make a difference.
To achieve our aims:
We have developed an outstanding curriculum that helps all children to succeed in their academic and personal development. Children are shown how to be effective learners with a growth mind-set that will equip them for life, giving pupils confidence to embrace challenges and handle set backs. We are committed to equity for all and this is reflected in the content of our curriculum, our ethos, and our commitment to anti-racist practices. We provide enriching arts and cultural experiences as part of our entitlement pledge that are fundamental to their cultural and holistic development. We strive to continually develop, innovate and grow as educators providing excellence in teaching and learning.
Hattoneers work together to create a safe, happy and fair world for everyone.
Value and respect everyone equally.
Behave with consideration and kindness.
Care for our environment

pageCache.pageTitle: Christopher Hatton Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's welcome
My name is Clare McBride, I am the headteacher at Christopher Hatton, it is my pleasure to welcome you to our school website, where I hope to give you a flavour of our school and show how we put our Hattoneer values into action. Christopher Hatton is a happy place with very high standards of behaviour, we achieve this not with stickers or gold stars but through strong positive relationships and our Hattoneer values. Our classrooms are places where your child will want to do well and contribute positively because of the sense of belonging, achievement and pride they feel in their learning.
At Christopher Hatton we want our pupils to be informed, articulate and empowered and live in a safe, happy, fair world. Our curriculum has a strong emphasis on learning TO talk and learning THROUGH talk. High quality teaching in the core subjects ensures that our pupils consistently achieve standards above national. We passionately believe in the value of the creative arts and provide a rich creative curriculum that allow pupils to excel in areas such as music, dance, visual arts through the use of specialist teachers and enrichment activities.
To find out more about our school click here to read our "Camden School Report"

pageCache.pageTitle: Christopher Hatton Primary School - Overview of SEND Information Report
pageCache.text:
overview of SEND Information Report
WHAT IS THE SEND INFORMATION REPORT
The Christopher Hatton Primary School SEND information report sets out what we provide for children and young people with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND) throughout their time with us and how we work with parents and carers. Our inclusion policy and provision map gives more detail about our day to day procedures. We review this report every year and welcome your input on how useful it is.
Please click here to view our SEND information report.
Camden Local Authority also publishes information for parents and carers of children with SEND on their website. Click here to access.
THE PURPOSE OF OUR SEND INFORMATION REPORT
The purpose of our SEND information report is to inform parents and carers about:
INCLUSION AT CHRISTOPHER HATTON
At Christopher Hatton the Inclusion Lead has overall responsibility for provision for children with special needs and disabilities. The role also includes ensuring that there is equality of opportunity and high achievement for children from different groups e.g. children with EAL (English as an additional language) and low-income families; for this reason the role is called the Inclusion Lead and includes the role of SENDCo. We have a strong reputation for inclusion at Christopher Hatton.
OUR VISION AND VALUES
At Christopher Hatton we believe that a “growth mindset” is one of the best assets a young person can have. This means that we place a high emphasis on learning how to learn and encourage the children to take risks in their learning, set their own challenges, embrace mistakes as learning opportunities and to understand that mastery comes from practice. We want our pupils to be informed, articulate and empowered. We place a high value on our communication with parents and carers, the first educators of our pupils and as such we welcome them in the classroom for the first 15 minutes on certain days of the week. We also know that the earlier we provide support for children with SEND, the more successful they will be and the more able they will be to cope with the challenges and responsibilities of modern life and to this end we strive to support children as soon as it is clear that they have a particular need.
AN INCLUSIVE SCHOOL FOR ALL
At Christopher Hatton Primary School we welcome pupils with special educational needs and disabilities, and make every effort to support them. All our classes are fully inclusive and we have high expectations for all our children. We aim to meet the needs of pupils with:
Specific learning difficulties
Mild learning difficulties
Social, emotional and mental health needs
Complex health needs
Communication difficulties, including autism
WHO TO CONTACT FOR MORE INFORMATION
All staff below can be contacted via email: admin@chrishatton.camden.sch.uk.

Secondary Transfers 2025
Primary to secondary school transfer
If your child is in Year 6 you need to start choosing a secondary school. I know this can be a daunting process but there is lots of help available. In addition to the information and events below, I will hold a meeting on Thursday 14th September at 3.45pm to help you through the process. Please be aware some schools require additional forms or may have specialist places available with interviews/auditions taking place before the October deadline.
Fortunately, Camden has great secondary schools. You can find out more by reading the brochures, attending the Moving on events, watching the short school films and by visiting on open days. Please take time to have a look, as a first step the latest guide to secondary schools in Camden can be accessed here
Secondary Schools in Camden admissions guide – applying for a Year 7 place
Your child will be due to start secondary school in September 2025 if they were born between 1 September 2013 and 31 August 2014. The next round of Year 7 applications for 2025 entry begins from 1 September 2024. You need to apply before the deadline of 31 October 2024.
Apply online for a Year 7 place from September 2024
School open days and evenings 2024
Camden secondary schools hold open days and evenings during September and October (and in November for sixth forms). These are a great way to find out more about the schools for yourself before applying. Download a poster with all the dates and times below:
Camden secondary schools - open events 2024 poster
Meet the Parents also hold informal forums for primary parents at local schools across the borough - see their timetable of events.
Short films about Camden secondary schools

Anti-Bullying
We are committed to providing a safe, happy and fair learning environment for all of our pupils. We promote an inclusive ethos that focuses on respecting one another and celebrating difference and diversity. Our staff develop strong, trusting relationships with the pupils and we believe this fosters trusting relationships where children can share concerns easily. We also hope that our frequent face to face communication with families also creates the same trust with you the parents.
Bullying and prejudice-based language of any kind, involving pupils, adults towards pupils, staff or parents are unacceptable and will not be tolerated at our school. We understand the devastating and lasting effect being bullied can have on some children and we will deal with all incidents equally seriously, quickly and effectively, whether it has taken place in or outside of school.
Preventing and tackling bullying is part of our work to support pupils’ social and emotional development and to be recognised as a healthy school.

Safeguarding
At Christopher Hatton we take the safeguarding of children extremely seriously.
If you are concerned about a child then please speak to one of our safeguarding team by calling the school office on 0207 278 4500 or find them in person.
Our of school hours you can call Camden's multi-agency safeguarding hub on 0207 974 4444. In emergencies please call the police for advice.
The safeguarding team at Christopher Hatton are:
Clare McBride the headteacher is the designated safeguarding lead
Kay McAllan is deputy safeguarding lead
Jennifer Smith is deputy safeguarding lead and our designated LAC teacher.
Useful resources to support you and your child to keep safe are available on the parent link section of our website.
We run regular internet safety workshops for parents; if you would like any advice on online safety please talk to Sarah or Clare.

English
At Christopher Hatton we teach a broad, balanced and creative English curriculum. We are focused on achieving excellent standards in oral communication, reading and writing. We want our pupils to question and critique all that they see and read. We want them to be able to put forward their ideas and express their opinions through speaking and writing. Real life experiences, drama, debate, rich texts and our topic based curriculum are all used to ignite interest and enthusiasm. We make sure that composition and grammar aspects of writing are taught contextually within the learning journey which leads towards a meaningful outcome. This may be written, spoken, performed, filmed, animated, or blogged. To view the English curriculum for your child, please go to the year group page and click on the topic overview.
Please click on the links below to find out more about how we teach different aspects of the English curriculum:

We have a dedicated, well stocked, library in school as well as book corners in every class. The library is open during lunchtimes for children to visit. History at Christopher Hatton School
Intent
Our aim is for all pupils to be informed, articulate and empowered:
In History this means the curriculum encourages pupils to find out about Britain’s past and that of the wider world. History is highly valued as part of our rich curriculum. It equips children with the knowledge and understanding of significant aspects of history and the skills they need to make connections to their own histories and to critically evaluate the sources of evidence which are used to make historical claims. Our history curriculum draws from and makes full use of the immediate and wider local area which enables children to develop a deep understanding of the rich history of their locality.
Informed
Children gain a coherent knowledge and understanding of Britain’s past and that of the wider world. They learn about diverse places and people and how they have shaped the world we live in today. Children are able to gain historical perspective through developing a growing sense of chronology and placing their knowledge into these timescales. They are able to use their knowledge to begin to understand the complexity of people’s lives, the processes of change, the diversity of societies and the relationships between different groups as well as the challenges they faced.
Articulate
Through the teaching of subject specific vocabulary and the opportunities for focussed talk during lessons, children develop their ability to speculate, make connections and interpret evidence to develop their historical understanding about the world and its people. We use activities such as ‘fed in facts’ to develop a deeper understanding and support historical recounts.
Empowered
Significant people and events which reflect the diversity of our community are included in our teaching to enable pupils to see themselves within the history curriculum. This is further supported through the inclusion of a parallel narrative to counter the predominantly white/Eurocentric focus often given. For example exploring the role and impact of black and Asian service men and women in the study of the Second World War.
Resources and materials are selected which provide a more accurate, more inclusive, and more intercultural representation of the past, we include historical figures of note from diverse backgrounds. We also identify where historical figures have demonstrated Hattoneer qualities such as perseverance and resilience. Children explore history within contexts that connect with their own lives e.g. significant events and people from the local area.
We teach our children to ask questions, think critically, evaluate evidence and arguments to enable them to develop perspective and judgment about the way the past is represented and the potential for bias in historical accounts. We make full use of the museums and galleries in our local area. These visits empower children to understand that these places belong to them. This sense of curiosity and fascination about the past is essential to fully engaging in a rich cultural life.
All children including those who have SEND or are disadvantaged are supported to fully access the history curriculum. This may include additional adult support or use of visuals or Widget symbols for instructions. Structured sentence stems and taught vocabulary scaffolds children in discussion.

Mathematics
Intent
Our aim is for all pupils to be informed, articulate and empowered:
In Maths this means children are engaged and inspired by a mastery teaching approach that enables all to make progress and achieve. Mathematical fluency and understanding of number are crucial to children’s future success and are taught in depth at Christopher Hatton. Oracy is a core element of our maths teaching to enable children to articulate their ideas clearly and develop a deeper understanding of the maths. We want children to leave Christopher Hatton being confident and enjoying maths.
Informed
Articulate
Empowered
Implementation
We use a Teaching for Mastery approach which rejects the idea that many children ‘just can’t do maths’. All children are encouraged by the belief that by working hard at maths they can succeed.
